title: Reasons for HDB BTO Applicants Not Booking A Flat When Invited to Do So
what_it_is: Reasons for HDB BTO Applicants Not Booking A Flat When Invited to Do So

sections.label: Flat non-selection consequences
sections.summary: From August 2023, applicants with one non-selection count face ballot or participation restrictions, with exemptions for limited choices and extenuating circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The most common reasons shared by applicants who did not book a flat when invited to do so, are as follows: firstly, their preferred units have been taken up; secondly, they have since decided to buy a resale flat; or thirdly, they have changed their minds and want to apply for flats in other sales exercises instead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: While there are different reasons for non-selection, such applicants do crowd out other home buyers who may have more urgent housing needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: From the August 2023 Build-To-Order (BTO) exercise, first-timers (FTs) with one non-selection count will be considered as second-timers (STs) for a year in the computer ballot; while STs with one non-selection count will not be allowed to participate in sales exercises for a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To be fair to applicants who are left with limited choices, HDB will not issue a non-selection count to applicants with 10 or fewer BTO flats, or five or fewer Sale of Balance flats, to choose from when their turn is due.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Where there are extenuating circumstances, HDB may exercise flexibility to waive the non-selection count.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Each appeal is evaluated on its own merits and appellants will need to provide documentary evidence to HDB to substantiate their case where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I shared earlier, when there are extenuating circumstances, HDB may exercise flexibility on a case-by-case basis.
